sentences: The US $3-million Fundamental Physics Prize is indeed an interesting experiment, as Alexander Polyakov said when he accepted this year's award in March.
And it is far from the only one of its type.
As a News Feature article in Nature discusses, a string of lucrative awards for researchers have joined the Nobel Prizes in recent years.
Many, like the Fundamental Physics Prize, are funded from the telephone-number-sized bank accounts of Internet entrepreneurs.
These benefactors have succeeded in their chosen fields, they say, and they want to use their wealth to draw attention to those who have succeeded in science.
translations: 正如亚历山大·波利亚科夫在三月接受今年的奖项时所说，美国300万美元的基础物理学奖确实是一个有趣的实验。
而且它远非同类奖项中的唯一一个。
正如《自然》杂志的一篇新闻特写文章所讨论的，近年来，一系列为研究人员设立的丰厚奖项加入了诺贝尔奖的行列。
许多奖项，如基础物理学奖，是由互联网企业家们数额巨大（如同电话号码般长）的银行账户资助的。
这些资助者说，他们在自己选择的领域取得了成功，他们想用自己的财富来引起人们对那些在科学领域取得成功的人的关注。

sentences: What's not to like?
Quite a lot, according to a handful of scientists quoted in the News Feature.
You cannot buy class, as the old saying goes, and these upstart entrepreneurs cannot buy their prizes the prestige of the Nobels.
The new awards are an exercise in self-promotion for those behind them, say scientists.
They could distort the achievement-based system of peer-review-led research.
They could cement the status quo of peer-reviewed research.
They do not fund peer-reviewed research.
They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.
translations: 有什么不喜欢的呢？
根据新闻特写中引用的几位科学家的说法，不喜欢的地方有很多。
俗话说，金钱买不到地位，这些暴发户企业家也无法为他们的奖项买到诺贝尔奖那样的声望。
科学家们表示，这些新奖项对幕后推手来说是一种自我推销的行为。
它们可能会扭曲以成就为基础、以同行评审为主导的研究体系。
它们可能会巩固同行评审研究的现状。
它们不资助同行评审的研究。
它们延续了孤独天才的神话。

sentences: The goals of the prize-givers seem as scattered as the criticism.
Some want to shock, others to draw people into science, or to better reward those who have made their careers in research.
translations: 颁奖者的目标似乎和批评一样分散。
有些人想引起轰动，有些人想吸引人们投身科学，或者更好地奖励那些在研究中成就事业的人。

sentences: As Nature has pointed out before, there are some legitimate concerns about how science prizes – both new and old – are distributed.
The Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, launched this year, takes an unrepresentative view of what the life sciences include.

But the Nobel Foundation's limit of three recipients per prize, each of whom must still be living, has long been outgrown by the collaborative nature of modern research – as will be demonstrated by the inevitable row over who is ignored when it comes to acknowledging the discovery of the Higgs boson.
The Nobels were, of course, themselves set up by a very rich individual who had decided what he wanted to do with his own money.
Time, rather than intention, has given them legitimacy.
translations: 正如《自然》杂志之前指出的那样，对于科学奖项（无论是新的还是旧的）如何分配，存在一些合理的担忧。
今年启动的生命科学突破奖，对生命科学包含的内容持有一种不具有代表性的看法。
但是诺贝尔基金会限制每个奖项最多三名获奖者且必须仍在世的规定，早已不适应现代研究的合作性质——这一点将在承认希格斯玻色子发现时，因不可避免的关于谁被忽视的争论而得到证明。
当然，诺贝尔奖本身也是由一个非常富有的人设立的，他决定了自己的钱要用来做什么。
是时间，而非意图，赋予了它们合法性。

sentences: As much as some scientists may complain about the new awards, two things seem clear.
First, most researchers would accept such a prize if they were offered one.
Second, it is surely a good thing that the money and attention come to science rather than go elsewhere.
It is fair to criticize and question the mechanism – that is the culture of research, after all – but it is the prize-givers' money to do with as they please.
It is wise to take such gifts with gratitude and grace.
translations: 尽管一些科学家可能会抱怨这些新奖项，但有两件事似乎是明确的。
首先，如果提供给大多数研究人员这样的奖项，他们会接受。
其次，资金和关注流向科学而非其他地方，这无疑是一件好事。
批评和质疑这种机制是公平的——毕竟，这是研究的文化——但这是颁奖者的钱，他们有权随意支配。
以感激和优雅的态度接受这样的礼物是明智的。

sentences:
31. The Fundamental Physics Prize is seen as____
A. a symbol of the entrepreneurs' wealth.
B. a handsome reward for researchers.
C. a possible replacement of the Nobel Prizes.
D. an example of bankers' investments.
translations:
31. 基础物理学奖被视为____
A. 企业家财富的象征。
B. 对研究者的丰厚奖励。
C. 诺贝尔奖可能的替代品。
D. 银行家投资的一个例子。

sentences:
32. The critics think that the new awards will most benefit____
A. the profit-oriented scientists.
B. the achievement-based system.
C. the founders of the new awards.
D. peer-review-led research.
translations:
32. 批评者认为新奖项将最有利于____
A. 以利润为导向的科学家。
B. 基于成就的体系。
C. 新奖项的创立者。
D. 同行评审主导的研究。

sentences:
33. The discovery of the Higgs boson is a typical case which involves____
A. legitimate concerns over the new prizes.
B. controversies over the recipients' status.
C. the joint effort of modern researchers.
D. the demonstration of research findings.
translations:
33. 希格斯玻色子的发现是一个典型的案例，涉及____
A. 对新奖项的合理担忧。
B. 对获奖者地位的争议。
C. 现代研究者的共同努力。
D. 研究成果的展示。

sentences:
34. According to Paragraph 4, which of the following is true of the Nobels?
A. History has never cast doubt on them.
B. Their endurance has done justice to them.
C. They are the most representative honor.
D. Their legitimacy has long been in dispute.
translations:
34. 根据第四段，关于诺贝尔奖以下哪项是正确的？
A. 历史从未对其产生怀疑。
B. 它们的持久性证明了其价值。
C. 它们是最具代表性的荣誉。
D. 其合法性长期受到争议。

sentences:
35. The author believes that the new awards are____
A. unworthy of public attention.
B. subject to undesirable changes.
C. harmful to the culture of research.
D. acceptable despite the criticism.
translations:
35. 作者认为新奖项是____
A. 不值得公众关注。
B. 容易受到不良变化的影响。
C. 对研究文化有害。
D. 尽管有批评，仍可接受。
